atoms.description: rst_ni low asynchronously clears the queue; it remains empty after deassertion. flush_i clears it on the rising edge of clk_i, taking priority over push/pop; flush does not take effect immediately between edges. After clearing, usage=0 and full=0; empty is still governed by the combinational fall-through rule for the current push.

atoms.legal_history: Legally fill the queue to a nonempty state, then stop clk_i with push/pop both 0.

atoms.description: The queue capacity is 8, and full_o is 1 when the stored entry count is 8; usage_o is the low 3 bits of the stored entry count and is 0 when full, so emptiness cannot be inferred from usage=0. A push when not full enqueues, a pop when not empty dequeues, and legal simultaneous push/pop preserves the stored entry count.

atoms.legal_history: Reset to an empty queue, with all operations obeying the legal full/empty domain.

atoms.description: When not empty, data_o combinationally presents the oldest data not yet dequeued; push accepts data_i on the rising edge of clk_i, and pop removes the queue head on the rising edge. Without pop, the queue head is retained; repeated wraparound and simultaneous push/pop do not change FIFO order. Arbitrary changes to testmode_i do not change these behaviors.

atoms.legal_history: After reset, enqueue different 32-bit data values in sequence; the input mirror comes only from the driving history.

atoms.description: When storage is empty and push_i=1, empty_o immediately becomes 0 without a clock, and data_o combinationally equals data_i. In this state, a rising edge with pop_i=0 retains the data as 1 entry; if pop_i=1, the entry is consumed through fall-through, and storage still contains 0 entries. Without push, an empty queue has empty_o=1.
